claim: A Fast pick reached through the entrance loads about 9.7k est. tokens of instructions before ranking a single entry (entrance 1.4k + roadmap menu 0.9k + pick.md 7.4k) — down 62% from the roughly 25.5k the same flow loaded before prompt assembly moved into craft-handoff.js and the roadmap skill split into branch files (entrance 1.3k + roadmap skill 10.8k + prompt-template.md 13.4k).

the Fast pick branch, rewritten around craft-handoff.js

the sprint flow, rewired onto craft-handoff.js
the canonical assembly source — no skill reads it directly anymore; craft-handoff.js and check-prompt.js read it at run time instead

render-sections.js resolves modelSuggestions: true (default false) — gates Call 5c and Call 6

aggregate.statistic: single deterministic computation over the checked-out repo (no dispersion — repeating it returns the same values)

limitations: bytes/4 is an estimate, not a tokenizer count — the real token count for any of these files depends on the model's actual tokenizer and will differ from the number here.

These numbers are what each flow's own file instructs a session to read, not what a live session actually loads — a real conversation carries the roadmap's own JSON, tool results, and prior turns on top of every number here.

roadmap-schema.md and model-fit.md are both conditional add-ons and are excluded from every flow's core total (files/bytes_total/est_tokens) above. roadmap-schema.md is excluded everywhere and appears only as optional_add_on, gated on the roadmap skill's own 'skim it if you need field semantics' invitation — it applies to fast_pick_via_entrance, add_task, correct_task, review_status, check_roadmap, init, and survey (not sprint or craft_prompt, whose files never mention it). model-fit.md is excluded everywhere and appears only as optional_add_on on fast_pick_via_entrance and craft_prompt, gated on render-sections.js resolving modelSuggestions: true, which defaults to false — no other flow reads it at all.

Editing any fixture listed above invalidates this record — validate-records.js fails on the sha256 mismatch rather than letting a stale number keep supporting a README claim; a corrected measurement needs a new record with supersedes pointing here.

The ~25,497 est. token before-figure the claim compares against was measured the same way against an earlier commit, but was never itself published as a record — it comes from an unpublished working measurement — so it is carried here as historical context only, not something this record's own command reproduces.

Recomputed from R-006 after the sprint flow was rewired onto craft-handoff.js. sprint no longer instructs a session to read prompt-template.md, so its flow total is its own SKILL.md alone and drops from 14,182 to 2995 est. tokens. No skill file reads prompt-template.md now; the two scripts that assemble and gate a handoff read it at run time.

environment.foreman_commit names the PARENT commit. This record ships in the same commit as the fixture edit it measures, so that commit sha cannot appear inside it; the fixture sha256 values above, not the commit, are what pin the bytes.
